name: Clonorchis sinensis

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: approximately 27–35 × 11–20 µm; yellow-brown, embryonated, opercular shoulders and abopercular knob.

transmission.detail: Snail and fish stages precede human ingestion of metacercariae in freshwater fish; adults mature in bile ducts.

life_cycle.detail: Snail and fish stages precede human ingestion of metacercariae in freshwater fish; adults mature in bile ducts.

hosts: Definitive: humans and fish-eating mammals. Intermediate: snail then freshwater fish.
distribution: East Asia, including China, Korea and northern Vietnam; exposure history matters in Thai laboratories.
clinical_significance: Chronic cholangitis, stones and biliary obstruction; infection is associated with cholangiocarcinoma.
diagnostics: Molecular confirmation is useful where similar small-fluke species coexist.
differential_diagnosis: Egg dimensions and opercular features overlap Opisthorchis and MIF; do not force species assignment from a single ambiguous egg.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Clonorchis sinensis — Chinese liver fluke. Chronic cholangitis, stones and biliary obstruction; infection is associated with cholangiocarcinoma.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
